# Common-q b4 contrasts on four public prefixes

Author: @radialmonster
Verified by: @radialmonster
Lead: #642
Variant: unassigned
Builds on: #32, #11, #267

## Claim
On four previously reported public 262144-token candidate prefixes, the equal-weight low4 b4=1-minus-b4=0 contrast is negative on common q support in all four. This is descriptive conditioning, not a causal adjustment or evidence of a physical gate. The earlier report uses the opposite 0-minus-1 direction.

## Original evidence
Lead #642 applied the fixed common-support reducer to the published 262144-token histograms on IDs 241, 1079, 4126 and 6343, with common q=0..8. The stored report SHA-256 is b1ded51f23cd5d431fc1076542740082de76592601004cddb2d3c3899f91201f. Exact means and local supports are reproduced below.

## Verification
After the lead was posted, fresh runs on those same four CC0 files reproduced the 262144-token histograms, endpoints and escape counts, and tested the predeclared wider 524288-token extent. All input files were previously exposed; this is wider-prefix verification by the same human, not independent captures. An independently written literal bit parser matched every q-by-b4 low3/low4 histogram and endpoint; an independently written exact Fraction reducer matched common/local supports, per-q contrasts and exclusions. Both parser paths share the TIFF locator.

At 524288 the 241 low4 common-support mean is positive and the other three are negative, so the all-negative claim is limited to the original extent; 1079 has a negative common-support mean and a positive local-support mean. Each extent recomputes its own common support: q=0..8 at 262144 and q=0..9 at 524288. The newly included q9 is sparse: b4=0/1 counts are 1/1, 59/38, 7/3 and 63/60 for 241, 1079, 4126 and 6343 respectively. Uniform strata weights can amplify sparse cells; the minimum group count was fixed at one.

Exact means use b4=1 minus b4=0. The last column counts positive / zero / negative common-stratum contrasts.

## Reproduce

At commit 33ddc259e8d508b7679808179030e4c912f05785 verify the stored report hash above and run:

```text
python -I -B tools/b4_common_q_support.py stats/lead32-q-stratified-b4-transfer.json
```

The report's four public names and SHA-256 values are in #32 comment 6480893109. The source probe uses stop 1/five suffix bits and no extra escape skip; selected q and b4 are candidate-token fields, not established codec state.


For fresh verification, set each FILE placeholder to the corresponding retained CC0 file and run this four-sample command at both token extents, saving the JSON output as REPORT:

```text
python -I -B tools/token_b4_gate_probe.py --q-stratified --tokens 262144 --sample 241 "Olympus - E-P3 - 16bit (4:3).ORF" FILE241 --sample 1079 "Olympus - E-PM1 - 16bit (4:3).ORF" FILE1079 --sample 4126 "Olympus - E-M10 Mark IV - 16bit (4:3).ORF" FILE4126 --sample 6343 "OM System - OM-5 - 16bit (4:3).ORF" FILE6343
python -I -B tools/b4_common_q_support.py REPORT
```

Repeat with `--tokens 524288`. Public file hashes are in #32 comment 6480893109 and #642.

## Limitations
The support is estimated from the same previously examined files, q is a candidate-token field, and neither the conditional contrasts nor sign changes under alternative support establish physical framing, a codec gate or significance. Separately justified field definitions and support choices on the existing corpus remain open.
